LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Range: Learn how soft docking works. Explore the optional weapons range, or head to the station and return later.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Range:
Takeoff, matching velocity and exterior work: you have learned the essentials. Congratulations!

There is also soft docking. Enable the docking indicators at the lower right of your PDA. Face two ports toward each other and overlap their outer diamonds; keep them aligned until the connection completes. Stop manual flight and use Organize transfer at the port to send people across.

Before collecting your new ship, I recommend visiting the weapons range southeast of the wreck. The western structure is the platform; the eastern one is its target. Follow the gold arrow and operate the entrance terminal; acknowledging its instructions unlocks the blast door.

Starbound developed kinetic and electromagnetic line shields for local combat. They have very different strengths and weaknesses from traditional guard domes. You may not have encountered them before your voyage. Experimenting here could save your life in a pirate fight.

Nothing here is an exam. Look around as long as you like, then reopen this guidance to arrange the handover. You can also collect the new ship first and visit the range later.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Unshielded:
All shields are off. The target has six layers of steel walls at the front. Fire the same type of cannon from the northern main and southern secondary sets. Compare the size and shape of the openings and the area damaged. Aim at intact armour for each shot so previous damage does not skew the comparison.

===CHEMICAL GUNS===

The propellant charge drives the projectile out of the barrel. More propellant or a lighter projectile gives it a higher muzzle velocity. Cooling systems vary between guns, so the same charge can put different demands on their cooling. If the charge is adjustable, loading more propellant generally generates more heat per shot.

Chemical guns can use two kinds of projectile head. The built-in magazine defaults to high-explosive steel and can be switched to armour-piercing uranium. Each ammunition type deals damage in a different way.

High-explosive steel detonates when it hits a structure. A heavier projectile produces a stronger and wider blast, with damage falling off away from the centre. The northern main set uses high-explosive rounds. Its rapid cannon is good at clearing broad areas of foundations and the equipment on them. Its heavy cannon can blast a wide opening in the outer armour for the rapid gun to exploit.

Armour-piercing uranium penetrates along its flight path. More propellant gives the projectile more energy and greater penetration. Measured relative to the firing ship's muzzle at launch, a heavier round leaves the barrel more slowly with the same kinetic energy at equal charge. What matters for damage is the kinetic energy relative to the point struck on the target. A slow round can still penetrate well if it meets a fast ship head-on. The southern secondary set uses armour-piercing rounds. Its rapid cannon is good at clearing exposed equipment and handles armour better than its high-explosive counterpart. Its heavy cannon punches a narrow, deep hole through several layers of armour.

Both heavy cannons use 48 units of propellant and 48 heads. At the same head count, the uranium round is heavier and leaves the muzzle more slowly.

===LASERS===

Lasers use no physical ammunition. At power 3 each pulse deals 48 structural damage to the cell it hits. Lasers are precise, use stored power and are good against exposed equipment. Their damage is confined to the point of impact, which limits their maximum damage compared with cannon fire.

===RAILGUN===

A railgun uses no propellant and few projectile heads, but it takes a great deal of power and can penetrate deeply.

Secondary group 4 is the central railgun. Its ten-cell barrel consists of the loader and nine accelerators, a practical size for a capital ship.

When fully powered, a shot at normal incidence against a stationary target uses 6,750 Wd and can destroy six steel gravship bulkheads or drain up to 5,000 guard capacity.

A heavy cannon at full charge can pierce three layers of steel bulkheads, but the round is relatively slow. Even in a salvo, it is difficult to hit the same point repeatedly. Three fully charged medium heavy cannons occupy about the same space as the railgun. A head-on salvo drains 864 capacity, leaving a full standard guard with 636.

Heavy cannon salvos are cheaper overall, but harder to land and less effective against guard shields. The railgun excels at deep penetration and breaking guard shields, though kinetic shields can disrupt its rounds.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Kinetic:
All three kinetic shields are set to {0}%. This column offers 0/20/100%. The central segment is straight and the flanks tilt 30 degrees. Compare different segments using one gun, then compare the two heavy cannons.

A kinetic shield applies normal impulse while preserving tangential velocity. At 0% there is no impulse, no per-hit fee and no automatic fragmentation. At 20% impulse is 72; at 100% it is 360. Heavier rounds receive less velocity change.

At normal incidence the shield changes speed and the round stays intact. If the shield slows a uranium round, penetration depends on its remaining kinetic energy relative to the point it strikes on the target. A steel shell that stays whole still detonates according to head mass if it hits. Sufficient lateral impulse can make a round tumble or tear it into three ordinary fragments or four rod fragments. Penetration falls sharply. Actual incidence depends on both trajectory and surface normal.

Rapid fire drains power through frequent hits, but strong shields can return light rounds with increased energy. Both heavy cannons load 48 units of propellant and 48 heads. The same impulse changes the velocity of the heavier southern uranium round less. Rail rods are especially vulnerable to oblique instability; the fixed central railgun against a straight segment does not demonstrate that.

Costs include base processing, requested impulse and positive work on the projectile. Underpayment funds only an affordable impulse, then determines the resulting shape and briefly disables the shield. Lasers, missiles and boarding craft pass through.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_GuardSingle:
Only the primary guard shield is enabled. Each generator starts with 750 regular and 750 emergency capacity; switching does not restore prior expenditure.

Guard stops attacks other than boarding craft if capacity is sufficient. A rail round with excess budget continues penetrating. Steel and uranium rounds from chemical guns both drain guard capacity according to their relative impact energy. An intact rail round uses its remaining energy to penetrate the hull after breaking a guard. Heavy cannons are poor suppressors. Rapid fire drains capacity frequently, continuous laser fire delays recovery, and railguns serve as opening shield breakers.

White is regular, red emergency. Recovery begins 3 seconds after the last regular-capacity expenditure at 6 points per second. Emergency hits do not restart that wait. Automatic rejoin is set to 10%. Emergency capacity needs silver: one restores three points; filling 750 requires 250 silver.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Guard:
All three guard generators cooperate. Initially each has 750 regular capacity, for a 2,250 shared pool, plus its own 750 emergency reserve. Switching does not refill them.

All three domes cover the frontal armour and cross the fixed rail lane. Their full shared regular pool plus three local emergency reserves can absorb 4,500 points of guard demand along that lane. The ten-cell railgun then has about 494 points of structural penetration left, which the six steel layers can stop. Compare with the shields disabled; switching never repairs armour or refills capacity. Regular costs are shared among participating generators on the same ship. Emergency capacity is local to the struck shield and cannot be borrowed remotely.

Regular recovery starts after 3 seconds at 6 points per second per generator, including during emergency use. At the 10% automatic rejoin setting, an empty generator can return with 75 points after about 15.5 seconds if regular capacity is not consumed again. Laser fire suppresses regular recovery, but emergency hits do not restart its wait. Watch each generator, not just the first surface disappearing.

You may head to the station without completing any demonstration.

LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Introduction:
Welcome to the Starbound Frontier range. Acknowledge these instructions to unlock the blast door.

CONTROLS
New player ships default to automatic fire control. This test platform starts with fire control disabled for safety. Select the platform in the sidebar and choose manual fire control to shoot. The northern turrets are the main set. Their rapid and heavy cannons use high-explosive steel. The southern turrets are the secondary set, with armour-piercing uranium in both cannons. By default, LEFT mouse fires main weapons and RIGHT mouse fires secondary weapons, with the pointer over the map. Groups 1/2/3 in each set select rapid cannon, heavy cannon and laser. The central fixed railgun uses uranium and is secondary group 4. Both sets start with group 1 enabled; enable only one group in one set when comparing results.

Both rapid cannons fire every 10 ticks. Both heavy cannons use 48 units of propellant and 48 heads. Both lasers use power 3, consume energy continuously and have no heat lock. Turrets have advanced auto-aim and need no gunner. The railgun cannot turn.

SAFETY
Turrets have a 90-degree eastward arc and 150-cell range, allowing shots at all three target shield segments. This restricts direction, not each shot to the target hull. The station is behind the platform; keep ships clear of the firing lane. Use manual fire against this allied target. You may switch active groups, but not weapon settings. Damaging or dismantling allied equipment costs goodwill.

ORDER
Northern columns run west to east: unshielded, kinetic, electromagnetic, guard. North to south, kinetic offers 0/20/100%, electromagnetic 0/50/100%, and guard single/cooperative. Compare armour first, then angles at a fixed strength. Switching never repairs or refills anything.

The fixed rail lane avoids generators and crosses six steel armour layers, bulkheads and five isolated empty batteries. Watch narrow deep penetration, not foundation immunity. The platform has an experimental 36,000 Wd bank, not a typical ship battery budget.

A TESTER’S WISH
Our testers joke: “If only this were a game with saves. We could save before testing and reload if we wrecked the target.” I am certainly not hinting at anything. You may head to the station without firing.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Electromagnetic:
All three target electromagnetic line shields are set to {0}% strength. Use the group 3 laser on the central segment and the two oppositely tilted 30-degree flanks. Watch the segmented beam path. This column runs north to south through 0%, 50% and 100%.

At 0%, only passive refraction applies, with no per-hit active-turn energy cost; maintaining the field still requires power. A normal-incidence beam stays straight, an oblique beam bends, and a sufficiently steep incidence may reflect passively. Shield tilt is not the actual incidence angle: the muzzle position and aim point also matter.

At 50%, the passive output turns up to another 90 degrees toward returning along the incoming path. At 100%, up to 180 additional degrees allow a full return if funded. Energy depends on the actual added turn, not merely the strength setting. Underpayment weakens the turn and briefly disables the line. The platform guard shield catches returning laser fire.

Only lasers are affected. Solid rounds, missiles and boarding craft pass through. Deflection does not delete a beam; it can still hit another surface, and weak deflection may not clear a large hull. Switching does not refill energy. Stored power and existing damage also influence the test.

Both range lasers use power 3: 6 Wd per shot, compared with 1.2 Wd for a full-strength return at normal incidence. EM counters lasers at relatively low cost. By default, left mouse fires northern main group 3 and right mouse fires southern secondary group 3.
